name: Zali Steggall
role: Australian Member of Parliament for Warringah
description: Australian parliamentarian assessed through climate legislation, market-based economic policy and rights protections.

axes.brief: She advocates representative democracy with parliamentary scrutiny, independent appeals and anti-corruption oversight.
axes.counterEvidence: Community engagement is not a documented requirement for direct votes on every national law.

axes.brief: She opposes unchecked visa powers and indefinite detention, supports whistleblowers and favours bounded hate-speech protection.
axes.counterEvidence: Rights protections coexist with safety regulation; criticism of rushed surveillance legislation does not prohibit all targeted investigation.

axes.brief: Her programme expressly celebrates diversity, Indigenous respect and inclusion within shared civic institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Social cohesion also involves participation in a common community rather than unlimited precedence for every separate cultural rule.

axes.brief: She seeks expanded humanitarian intake, fair citizenship pathways and an end to indefinite refugee detention.
axes.counterEvidence: Criticism of collective exclusion does not remove individual security checks or every visa condition.

qualifications.8: Housing pressure and benefits from entry give competing considerations.
qualifications.12: Education and lawful residence conditions do not establish an automatic graduation entitlement.

axes.brief: Her rights and regional-stability priorities suggest diplomacy and defensive preparedness rather than expansive intervention.

axes.brief: She supports international climate and humanitarian cooperation alongside Australian constitutional accountability.

qualifications.11: Retaliation and cost-of-living concerns pull in different directions.

axes.brief: She supports private production and targeted clean-energy industrial strategy, with caps on annual rent increases.
axes.counterEvidence: Rent regulation is sector-specific; ending fossil subsidies differs from opposing all government investment.

axes.brief: Her early tax positions protect investment incentives and small-business income while her current programme expands affordability and social inclusion.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposition to 2019 Labor tax proposals should not erase later housing reforms; exact wealth and inheritance transfer mechanisms remain uncertain.

qualifications.8: Work incentives and social protection conflict under a blanket time limit.
qualifications.10: Fiscal restraint and adequate benefits both matter.

axes.brief: Civil equality and anti-discrimination are articulated without religious approval over government.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal identity is unestablished; civil neutrality is not abolition of every inherited religious festival.

qualifications.14: Religious and charitable activity overlap, without an explicit exemption proposal.

axes.brief: She supports gender pay equity, shared parenting, LGBTQ rights and equal recognition.
axes.counterEvidence: Contemporary equal recognition does not settle the value of all non-discriminatory traditions.

qualifications.16: Historical continuity can be valued without a universal preservation obligation.

axes.counterEvidence: National leadership provides support to local councils rather than abolishing local powers.
